name: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series
source_notes: Verified against a shallow clone of the OWASP/CheatSheetSeries GitHub repo (last commit 2026-10-04), the source of cheatsheetseries.owasp.org.
caveats: Continuously updated series with no edition or release date; content reflects the repo as of 2026-10-04 (137 sheets). Only the sheets distilled in the research notes are included.
Sheets named in the notes without rule content are not included: MCP Security, LLM Prompt Injection Prevention, Webhook Security, Software Supply Chain Security.

Transport Layer Protection Cheat Sheet is DEPRECATED in favor of the Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet; Abuse Case Cheat Sheet is archived and should not be used for rules. Neither is included as an item.
No OWASP cheat sheet covers Supabase or Firebase; RLS appears only as generic Postgres guidance in the Multi-Tenant Security sheet. Supabase/Firebase rules must cite vendor docs.

Detection entries prefixed "(inferred) " are reinhardt mappings not literally in the sheet; unprefixed entries map directly to sheet text. csurf deprecation and cors package default behavior were not verified.
Only the Authorization sheet carries an explicit CWE reference in the notes (CWE-209); other cwe arrays are empty.
Detail extraction was partial: Secure Coding with AI (section headings only), Multi-Tenant Security, CI/CD Security and OS Command Injection Defense summaries are thinner than the others.
Item URLs follow the standard https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/<File_Name>.html pattern; whether the rendered site lags the repo was not checked.

items.name: JSON Web Token Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance for issuing and validating JWTs safely: algorithm pinning, trusted key selection, strong HMAC secrets and claim validation.
prevention: Reject "alg":"none" tokens.
Hard-code the accepted algorithms and do not mix public-key signature and MAC algorithms.
Never trust header-supplied key material (jku, x5u, x5c, kid); pick keys bound to the validated issuer.
Generate HMAC secrets with a CSPRNG, at least the hash output size, never a password or published value.
Validate exp, nbf, iss and aud.
Remember signed JWTs are not confidential; use JWE when claims must be secret.

static: jwt.verify(token, key) with no algorithms option
algorithms containing 'none' or mixing HS* with RS*/ES*
(inferred) jwt.decode() result used in an auth decision
jwt.sign(..., 'literal') with a short string-literal secret
review: Key rotation and issuer trust configuration

items.name: Password Storage Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to store passwords with slow, salted hashing algorithms and recommended work factors.
prevention: Hash passwords; never encrypt them or store plaintext.
Prefer Argon2id with at least m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1 (or an equivalent setting).
scrypt: N=2^17, r=8, p=1; bcrypt only for legacy, with work factor 10+ and a 72-byte input limit.
PBKDF2 (FIPS): at least 600,000 iterations with HMAC-SHA-256.
Do not use fast hashes such as MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 for passwords.
Use a unique salt per password; store any optional pepper separately (vault/HSM).
Compare hashes with constant-time functions.

static: (inferred) === used to compare a hash or token (use crypto.timingSafeEqual)

items.name: Session Management Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on generating, transporting, storing and renewing session identifiers.
prevention: Generate session IDs with a CSPRNG and at least 64 bits of entropy.
Set Secure and HttpOnly on session cookies; SameSite is defense in depth, not a CSRF replacement.
Prefer the __Host- cookie prefix for session IDs.
Do not store tokens, session IDs, JWTs or refresh tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage; use HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookies or a BFF.
Renew the session ID on any privilege change, at minimum at login.

static: res.cookie(name, v, opts) lacking httpOnly, secure or sameSite
express-session/cookie-session with cookie.secure false or missing, or a hard-coded secret

items.name: Authentication Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on password policy, error messaging, transport and protection against automated attacks during authentication.
prevention: Treat passwords under 8 characters as weak with MFA and under 15 without MFA; allow at least 64 characters.
Return generic errors for login, reset and registration to prevent user enumeration, and watch timing differences.
Send passwords only over TLS.
Require re-authentication for sensitive features.
Protect against automated attacks with rate limiting and MFA.

static: (inferred) Login route with no rate-limit middleware
Distinct "user not found" vs "wrong password" responses

items.name: Authorization Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Principles for enforcing authorization: least privilege, deny by default and per-request checks on the server.
prevention: Enforce least privilege.
Deny by default.
Validate permissions on every request.
Ensure lookup IDs are not accessible even when guessed.
Enforce authorization checks on static resources.
Exit safely when authorization fails, without exposing logs or debug output.
Never rely on client-side access control as the deciding control.

static: (inferred) Role/admin checks only in React components (e.g. user.role === 'admin') with no server check
(inferred) Route handlers with DB writes and no auth middleware

items.name: Insecure Direct Object Reference Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to prevent users from accessing objects by manipulating identifiers.
prevention: Implement access control checks for each object.
Scope lookups to the current user (e.g. current_user.projects.find(id)).
Derive the user from the session rather than IDs in the URL or body.
Treat complex IDs such as GUIDs only as defense in depth.

static: (inferred) findById(req.params.id) / findUnique({ where: { id: req.params.id } }) / supabase.from(t).select().eq("id", param) with no owner predicate
(inferred) userId taken from req.body/req.query instead of the session

items.name: Mass Assignment Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to prevent clients from setting object fields they should not control via automatic binding.
prevention: Use DTOs that contain only editable fields.
Allowlist bindable fields (e.g. pick safe fields from req.body).
Use blocklisting only as an alternative when allowlisting is impractical.
Remember DTOs and allowlists do not replace authorization.

static: Object.assign(entity, req.body) or {...req.body} passed to an ORM
review: Which fields are safe per role

items.name: Input Validation Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on validating input with allowlists and schemas at trust boundaries.
prevention: Prefer allowlist over denylist validation.
Apply request size limits before buffering or parsing, and configure parser depth limits.
Use a maintained parser, then validate against a schema.
Do not rely on client-only checks or trust internal sources or upload metadata.
Avoid "cleaning" input and logging rejected input verbatim.

static: (inferred) API route handlers using req.body.* without zod/yup/joi/valibot or similar validation

items.name: SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Ranked defenses against SQL injection, led by prepared statements.
prevention: Use prepared statements (parameterized queries).
Use stored procedures only when they contain no dynamic SQL.
Allowlist-validate table and column names that must be dynamic.
Treat escaping all user input as strongly discouraged.

static: (inferred) Supabase .rpc to SQL functions building dynamic EXECUTE format(...)
(inferred) Swift sqlite3_exec / sqlite3_prepare with string interpolation

items.name: Cross Site Scripting Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Output encoding and framework guidance for preventing XSS, including framework escape hatches.
prevention: Avoid framework escape hatches such as React dangerouslySetInnerHTML, Angular bypassSecurityTrustAs* and Lit unsafeHTML with unsanitized HTML.
Validate URL values even where frameworks block javascript: URLs.
Avoid eval and string-based setTimeout/setInterval.
Sanitize HTML with DOMPurify and keep it patched.

static: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: X }} where X is not wrapped in DOMPurify.sanitize
(inferred) marked/markdown-it output with html: true fed to the DOM
(inferred) iOS WKWebView.loadHTMLString with interpolated user data

items.name: DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to avoid DOM-based XSS by keeping untrusted data out of dangerous DOM sinks.
prevention: Populate the DOM with untrusted data via textContent.
Avoid innerHTML, document.write/writeln and event-handler attributes for untrusted data.
Never pass strings to setTimeout, setInterval or Function.

static: document.write( fed from location.*, URLSearchParams or postMessage data
review: Data flow from sources to sinks at runtime

items.name: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Defenses against CSRF for stateful and stateless applications.
prevention: Use the framework's built-in CSRF protection.
Otherwise use synchronizer tokens (stateful) or signed double-submit cookies (stateless); avoid naive double-submit.
Reject non-safe methods when Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site.
Use custom request headers for AJAX/API calls; treat SameSite as defense in depth.
Never use GET for state-changing operations.

static: (inferred) app.get( handlers that perform DB writes or deletes
(inferred) Cookie-session Express apps with POST routes and no CSRF/origin middleware
review: Effective CSRF protection across all state-changing routes

items.name: Server-Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Defenses against SSRF for both known-destination and arbitrary-destination fetch features.
prevention: For known targets, allowlist domains/IPs with strict comparison.
Disable redirect following in the HTTP client.
Validate resolved IPs to resist DNS rebinding, then connect to the validated IP.
For arbitrary targets, allow only HTTP/HTTPS, block private/internal IPs and build requests only from validated parts.
Segment the network and migrate to AWS IMDSv2; use deny-lists (e.g. 169.254.169.254) only as a last resort.
In Next.js keep images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP off and define images.remotePatterns tightly.

static: fetch(req.query.url | req.body.url), axios.get(userInput), got(...), http.get(...) with a tainted URL
next.config remotePatterns: [{ hostname: '**' }] or dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true
review: Network egress and metadata endpoint access

items.name: Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to avoid open redirects and forwards.
prevention: Avoid redirects and forwards where possible.
Do not accept the destination URL as user input.
Map a short ID or token to the destination server-side.
Use a local-only helper for return URLs.
Allowlist parsed scheme, host and port for external destinations.

items.name: File Upload Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Controls for accepting, validating and storing uploaded files safely.
prevention: Allowlist extensions and do not trust the Content-Type header.
Generate filenames server-side and limit filename length and charset.
Set a file size limit.
Allow only authorized users to upload and CSRF-protect the upload.
Store files outside the webroot or on a separate server.
Beware double extensions, null bytes and case tricks; re-encode images and strip metadata; avoid ZIP uploads.

static: (inferred) multer({ dest }) / multer({ storage }) without limits.fileSize or fileFilter
(inferred) file.originalname used in a filesystem path
(inferred) Supabase Storage bucket created public: true for user uploads
review: AV/CDR scanning and content validation depth

items.name: REST Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Security guidance for REST APIs covering transport, access control, tokens, API keys, methods, content types and errors.
prevention: Serve only over HTTPS and enforce access control at each endpoint.
Do not accept unsecured JWTs (alg none) or let the token header pick the verification algorithm.
Require API keys on every request, return 429 when rate limits are exceeded, and do not rely only on API keys for sensitive resources.
Restrict HTTP methods and validate request content types; protect management endpoints.
Return generic errors without stack traces or technical details.
Keep passwords, tokens and API keys out of URLs.

items.name: Node.js Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Security practices for Node.js applications, including Express configuration, dangerous APIs and dependency hygiene.
prevention: Set request size limits and do not block the event loop.
Validate input, escape output and protect against brute force and CSRF.
Use helmet for security headers and remove X-Powered-By.
Set cookie flags and only return necessary data.
Avoid eval, child_process.exec with input, and node:vm as a security boundary; watch fs paths for traversal.
Avoid evil regexes, keep packages updated and run security linters.

static: express() app with no helmet import
fs.readFile(path.join(base, req.params.x)) without normalization or prefix check
review: Event-loop blocking and runtime error handling

items.name: JavaScript and TypeScript Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Language-level security guidance for JavaScript and TypeScript code in browsers and servers.
prevention: Never build code from strings: use JSON.parse, not eval; enforce no-eval, no-implied-eval and no-new-func.
Omit 'unsafe-eval' from CSP script-src.
Build the DOM with textContent/createElement and use Trusted Types without a permissive default policy.
Avoid ReDoS-prone regexes and cap input length.
For postMessage, check event.origin against an allowlist and never send sensitive data to "*".
Validate untrusted data at trust boundaries with a runtime schema; TypeScript types are erased.
Reject __proto__, constructor and prototype keys in merges.

items.name: Prototype Pollution Prevention Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to prevent attackers from modifying JavaScript object prototypes via untrusted keys.
prevention: Use Map/Set instead of object literals for untrusted keys.
Use Object.create(null) when an object is required.
Freeze or seal prototypes.
Use Node --disable-proto=delete as defense in depth.
Never pass untrusted input to recursive merge or set-by-path helpers.

static: Custom recursive merge functions lacking a __proto__ guard

items.name: Next.js Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Next.js-specific guidance on proxy/middleware auth, Server Actions, environment variables and configuration.
prevention: Do not make proxy/middleware the only authorization layer (cf. CVE-2025-29927).
Treat every Server Action as a client-callable POST: validate input and authorize inside it.
Return only authorized fields from Server Actions and keep serverActions.allowedOrigins narrow.
Use NEXT_PUBLIC_ only for intentionally public values; mark sensitive modules server-only.
Protect revalidatePath/revalidateTag, keep productionBrowserSourceMaps off and never run next dev in production.
Validate env-derived hosts at startup and fail closed.

static: NEXT_PUBLIC_* names matching SECRET, SERVICE_ROLE, PRIVATE, TOKEN, PASSWORD or *_KEY (excluding PUBLISHABLE_KEY/ANON_KEY)
'use server' functions with no auth call
review: Authorization inside each action and route

items.name: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on storing, rotating, injecting and detecting secrets across applications and pipelines.
prevention: Centralize secrets, automate rotation, apply least-privilege access and audit use.
Never hard-code secrets, including in Docker ENV/ARG or build-time env.
Detect secrets in the IDE or pre-commit, using several tools that balance entropy and format detection.
Prefer dynamic or short-lived secrets.
On leak, revoke, then rotate, then delete, then log.
Prefer mounted volumes or sidecars over env vars for container secrets.

static: High-entropy literals and known prefixes (sk_live_, sb_secret_, AKIA, service_role JWT payload)
Secrets in Info.plist or Swift string constants

items.name: NPM Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Practices for safely consuming and publishing npm packages.
prevention: Avoid publishing secrets: .npmignore overrides .gitignore when both exist.
Enforce the lockfile (npm ci, yarn install --frozen-lockfile).
Consider ignoring run-scripts and audit dependencies.
Enable 2FA and minimize tokens.
Watch for typosquatting, AI-hallucinated package names (slopsquatting) and dependency confusion.
Verify documentation examples before copying them.

static: Dependencies not resolvable on the registry or newly published (optional network check)

items.name: HTTP Headers Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Recommended values for security-relevant HTTP response headers.
prevention: Send X-Frame-Options: DENY or CSP frame-ancestors.
Do not set X-XSS-Protection, or set it to 0.
Send X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
Send Strict-Transport-Security with a long max-age, includeSubDomains and preload.
Remove Server and X-Powered-By; do not use deprecated Expect-CT or HPKP.
Set specific origins in Access-Control-Allow-Origin rather than *, except for truly public APIs.

static: (inferred) vercel.json lacking a headers block (low severity)

items.name: Content Security Policy Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to deploy a strict, nonce- or hash-based Content Security Policy.
prevention: Use a strict nonce- or hash-based policy such as script-src 'nonce-...' 'strict-dynamic'.
Make nonces unique per response.
Do not auto-add nonces to every script tag in middleware.
Set object-src 'none'.
Use frame-ancestors instead of X-Frame-Options.

items.name: HTML5 Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on HTML5 features including CORS, postMessage and web storage.
prevention: Allow only selected trusted domains in Access-Control-Allow-Origin; never * or blindly reflected Origin for sensitive content.
Specify an exact target origin in postMessage, not *.
Check message origin by exact FQDN match, not indexOf.
Avoid keeping sensitive data in localStorage; prefer sessionStorage when persistence is not needed.

static: cors({ origin: true | '*', credentials: true }) or origin: (o, cb) => cb(null, true)

items.name: Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on algorithms, modes, randomness and key handling for data at rest.
prevention: Use AES with a 128-bit or larger (ideally 256-bit) key in authenticated modes (GCM/CCM).
Do not use ECB outside very specific circumstances.
Use RSA-OAEP for RSA encryption.
Never reuse an IV with the same key.
Use CSPRNGs: Node crypto.randomBytes/randomInt/randomUUID; Apple SecRandomCopyBytes or arc4random.
Do not use UUID v1 for secrets.

items.name: Transport Layer Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on TLS versions, cipher suites and HTTPS enforcement; supersedes the deprecated Transport Layer Protection Cheat Sheet.
prevention: Default to TLS 1.3, allow TLS 1.2 for compatibility, and disable TLS 1.0/1.1.
Use AEAD cipher suites.
Redirect HTTP to HTTPS and use HSTS.
On iOS, use App Transport Security and always use HTTPS.

static: http:// API base URLs in client or Swift code
(inferred) URLSessionDelegate that accepts any server trust

items.name: Logging Cheat Sheet
items.summary: What to log, what never to log, and how to protect log integrity.
prevention: Do not log session IDs, access tokens, passwords, connection strings, keys, card or bank data, sensitive PII or source code; remove, mask, hash or encrypt them.
Sanitize event data against log injection (CR, LF, delimiters).
Log authentication, authorization and session failures, including suspicious JWT validation failures.

static: (inferred) Swift print/NSLog/os_log with token or password values

items.name: Error Handling Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to handle unexpected errors with a global handler that returns generic responses.
prevention: Configure a global error handler for unexpected errors.
Return a generic response to clients.
Log error details server-side only.

static: (inferred) Express apps without a 4-argument error middleware

items.name: Denial of Service Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Application and infrastructure measures against resource-exhaustion attacks.
prevention: Limit file upload size and extensions and total request size.
Prevent input-based resource allocation and input-driven loops.
Beware of user lockout being abused as DoS.
Rate limit at infrastructure or application level.
Set minimum ingress data rates and timeouts.

static: (inferred) limit/take read from req.query without a cap
(inferred) No express-rate-limit (or similar) on auth or AI-proxy endpoints

items.name: Third Party JavaScript Management Cheat Sheet
items.summary: How to reduce risk from third-party scripts such as tags and analytics.
prevention: Mirror third-party scripts in-house where possible.
Use Subresource Integrity.
Transmit scripts securely.
Sandbox third-party code; a data layer is not a sandbox because tag managers can run custom JS.

items.name: OS Command Injection Defense Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Defenses against OS command and argument injection.
prevention: Avoid calling OS commands directly; prefer library APIs.
Escape values for the target OS when commands are unavoidable.
Use parameterization together with input validation.
Guard against argument injection as well as command injection.

items.name: Mobile Application Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Mobile app guidance, including iOS-relevant rules on server-side enforcement, credential storage and transport.
prevention: Perform authentication and authorization server-side; assume client-side controls can be bypassed.
Do not hard-code credentials or store user passwords on the device.
Use the Keychain and Secure Enclave for sensitive storage.
Do not use spoofable device identifiers for authentication and do not allow 4-digit PINs.
Avoid caching, logging or snapshotting sensitive data; use platform crypto APIs.
Use ATS, always use HTTPS, avoid sensitive data in plist files, and require auth for sensitive App Intents.

static: (inferred) API keys or secret literals in Swift
(inferred) UIDevice.current.identifierForVendor used as an auth credential

items.name: Secure Coding with AI Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Risks specific to AI-assisted coding, such as hallucinated or outdated dependencies, rules files, fabricated tests and markdown/Unicode injection.
prevention: Check AI-suggested dependencies exist and are legitimate (hallucinated dependencies).
Check suggested dependency versions for known CVEs.
Review AI rules files as part of the codebase.
Watch for fabricated or deleted tests.
Guard against Markdown/Unicode injection.

(inferred) Outdated dependency versions with known CVEs

items.name: Multi-Tenant Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Guidance on tenant isolation, including PostgreSQL row level security as a database-enforced boundary.
prevention: Enable row level security on tenant tables.
Force row level security so table owners are also subject to it.
Create tenant-isolation policies keyed on the current tenant ID.

items.name: CI/CD Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Practices for securing source control, pipelines and their dependencies and secrets.
prevention: Avoid auto-merge and require reviews that cannot be bypassed.
Use signed commits and MFA.
Pin dependencies and verify hashes; sign artifacts (e.g. Sigstore).
Detect secrets with tools such as git-leaks and git-secrets and keep secrets in vaults.
Avoid Docker --privileged, scope npm packages, commit .npmrc and never log secrets.

items.name: Docker Security Cheat Sheet
items.summary: Rules for securing Docker hosts, daemons, images and containers.
prevention: Keep host and Docker updated and never expose the daemon socket (TCP or mounted docker.sock).
Set a non-root USER and run rootless where possible.
Drop all capabilities, never use --privileged, and set no-new-privileges.
Bind ports to 127.0.0.1 where appropriate, limit resources and use seccomp/AppArmor/SELinux.
Use read-only filesystems and Docker secrets.
Lint and scan images (Trivy/Grype, secret scanners) and produce SBOMs and signatures.
